name: Jephthah
title: Judge of Gilead
summary: Jephthah was a Gileadite warrior and judge in Israel who led the people to victory over the Ammonites. He is best known for his foolish vow to God, which had tragic consequences for his only daughter. Despite his difficult background as the son of a prostitute, he was used by God to deliver Israel.

keyEvents.title: Cast Out by His Brothers
keyEvents.description: Jephthah was driven out by his half-brothers because he was the son of a prostitute woman, and settled in the land of Tob where he gathered a band of adventurers around him.

keyEvents.title: Called to Lead Israel
keyEvents.description: When the Ammonites threatened Israel, the elders of Gilead brought Jephthah back and made him their army commander and leader to fight against the enemy.

keyEvents.title: Negotiations with the King of Ammon
keyEvents.description: Jephthah first tried to resolve the conflict diplomatically by sending messengers to the king of Ammon and arguing for Israel's right to the land.

keyEvents.title: The Fatal Vow
keyEvents.description: Before the battle against the Ammonites, Jephthah made a rash vow to the Lord to offer as a sacrifice whatever came out of his house first if he won victory.

keyEvents.title: Victory over the Ammonites
keyEvents.description: The Spirit of the Lord came upon Jephthah, and he struck down the Ammonites with a great blow, capturing twenty towns, so that the Ammonites were humbled before the Israelites.

keyEvents.title: The Tragedy of His Daughter
keyEvents.description: Jephthah's only child, his daughter, came out to meet him dancing after the victory. In deep sorrow, Jephthah fulfilled his vow, and his daughter was given two months to mourn her virginity.
